name: Wall, diagonal run
description: Diagonal Stone Wall (point 41, m-hradby-diagonala). diagonal: a tile in the middle of a run – a band turned 45°, as wide on screen as the straight wall (its sides run through the tile's side corners), corner to corner, parapets on both long sides. elbow: the tile where a run ends (at a straight wall or free) – the wall block and half of the band in one piece; the outline bends at the block's corners and never crosses the wall. All drawn on the tile centre. Made by Claude with the wall-kit generator at the owner's request (15 Nov 2026); waits for the owner's approval.

variants.name: Run down the screen
variants.notes: Towards grid (x+1, y+1). On screen the wall runs straight down, seen from its end.

variants.name: Run across the screen
variants.notes: Towards grid (x+1, y−1). On screen the wall runs straight across, seen from its face.

variants.name: Elbow NE
variants.notes: End of a diagonal run: the block and half the band leaving through its NE corner (towards grid (x+1, y−1)).

variants.name: Elbow SE
variants.notes: End of a diagonal run: the block and half the band leaving through its SE corner (towards grid (x+1, y+1)).

variants.name: Elbow SW
variants.notes: End of a diagonal run: the block and half the band leaving through its SW corner (towards grid (x−1, y+1)).

variants.name: Elbow NW
variants.notes: End of a diagonal run: the block and half the band leaving through its NW corner (towards grid (x−1, y−1)).
